what_this_is: The Workshop rows of the measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging folder: scripts the person's AI runs on their computer to find when one character of a show speaks (voice and pitch), list what it says, measure how the show stages it, sum its time per video against the views, count the show's running jokes and code the comments about it. Every show, character, number and word is the person's settings row.

payload.label: Catalog a channel's videos by format, with views against the channel's rolling baseline (runs on your computer)
payload.job: List every video of a YouTube channel with its format (episode, side piece, compilation, members-only, short, or a series of its own) and how its views compare with the nearby videos of the same format
payload.description: Reads <youtube_folder>/flat/<channel>-videos.json and -shorts.json (yt-dlp flat playlist dumps) and, when present, <id>.info.json in captions/, videos/ or comments/ for the exact upload date, likes and comments. A video's format: short for the shorts list; the format of the first of the person's series_prefixes its lower-case title starts with; compilation when the title holds one of compilation_words; members-only with no views; side when side_pattern matches the title or it is under 3 minutes; else episode. Its baseline is the median views of the 10 same-format videos on each side in list order. Writes <data_folder>/catalog.tsv.

payload.label: Find when one character speaks in a show's recordings, by voice and pitch (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Find every stretch where one character of a show speaks, in all of its recordings, from a few stretches the person labels, even when the character is a cast member's own voice pitched up
payload.description: step embed: windows of 1.5 s every 0.5 s of a recording, each with a speaker embedding (pyannote wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet34-LM, from the local model cache), its median pitch and loudness, embedding only the windows high enough to be the character. step seed: add the windows inside the stretches the person names ("a-b,a-b") to <data_folder>/voice/seeds.npz with a label. step score: a logistic model on the seeds finds this recording's confident windows of the character among those that pass the pitch gate (at least the smaller of gate_max_hz and gate_pitch_ratio x the recording's median pitch); their mean embedding is the character's voice in this recording, and a gated window whose cosine to it is above voice_cosine_min is the character; neighbouring windows become turns, written as <id>.turns.json. step batch: embed and score every catalog video of batch_format_order not yet scored, from <audio_folder>/<audio_file>. step rescore: score every recording again with the current seeds. The label, gates and formats are the person's settings (character_label, embed_min_pitch_hz, embed_pitch_ratio, gate_pitch_ratio, gate_max_hz, voice_cosine_min, batch_format_order, audio_file). do-work/check_seed_model.py and check_voice_finder.py check it on recordings it did not learn from: leave one labelled recording out and count window precision and recall.

output_schema.description: {"result": ...}: embed {embeddings, windows, loud_windows, embedded}; seed {seeds, added, counts}; score {id, duration_s, character_s, turns, json}; batch {scored, failed}; rescore {scored}.

needs: python 3 with numpy, scikit-learn, librosa, torch and pyannote.audio
the speaker model pyannote/wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet34-LM in the local Hugging Face cache
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer. Read their settings row (records:read record:setting:measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>) into a file and pass it as settings_record. Ask them for two or three recordings where they know when the character speaks; embed those, seed the character's stretches with character_label and a few stretches of other high voices with another label, then run check_seed_model.py and check_voice_finder.py with the same data_folder and tell them the precision and recall per recording before running batch over the catalog. show/show_turns.py prints each turn with its caption words, to check by reading.

verify.requires: python 3 with numpy, scikit-learn, librosa, torch and pyannote.audio, ffmpeg, and the pyannote speaker model in the local cache

payload.label: Find the stretches of a recording spoken in a character's high pitch band (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Find where a recording has speech in a high pitch band, as a first look for a character voiced well above the rest of the cast
payload.description: librosa yin pitch every 25 ms with a periodicity voicing test; runs of voiced frames in the person's band (pitch_run_band_low_hz to pitch_run_band_high_hz) of at least 0.5 s, joined across 1.2 s gaps, kept when half their voiced frames are in the band. Writes <out_dir>/<id>.json (the runs with their median pitch) and <id>.f0.npy. Pitch alone also catches every other high voice; find-when-a-character-speaks tells them apart.

payload.label: Count a character's turns from the speaker marks in captions and the pitch of each turn (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Count a character's turns in each episode a second, independent way: the captions' speaker-change marks, and whether each marked turn is spoken high
payload.description: For each episode in <data_folder>/catalog.tsv with <youtube_folder>/captions/<id>.en.json3 holding at least five '>>' marks and an <id>.emb.npz (do-work/find_voice.py embed) in <data_folder>/voice or extra_voice_folders: a marked turn (to the next mark, at most 30 s) whose median window pitch is at least ratio (else the settings' caption_turn_pitch_ratio) times the episode's median pitch is the character's. Writes <data_folder>/character-caption-turns.tsv with the turns, seconds and seconds in the first 5 minutes.

payload.label: List every caption line a character says, with the second it starts (runs on your computer)
payload.job: List every caption line spoken inside a character's turns, with the video and second, for quoting
payload.description: Reads every <data_folder>/voice/<id>.turns.json (find-when-a-character-speaks) and the video's captions (the first of <youtube_folder>/captions or videos/<id>.en.json3, .en-orig.json3, .en*.json3, then <data_folder>/../raw/<id>.en.json3); a caption line counts when at least half of it lies inside a turn. Writes <data_folder>/character-lines.tsv (id, date, format, second, turn, text). Lines are auto-captions: the spelling is YouTube's.

payload.label: Measure how a video stages a character's turns: cuts, shot lengths and music stop-downs (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Measure how a video is cut and scored around a character's turns: whether a cut lands on the turn, how short the shots are inside the exchanges, and whether the music stops just before
payload.description: For each id: from <youtube_folder>/measure/<id>/rhythm.json (shots) and earshot-timeline.txt (GAP drop lines) and <data_folder>/voice/<id>.turns.json: the share of turns with a picture cut within 0.5 s of their start against chance, the median shot inside the character's exchanges (turns within 8 s, padded 2 s) against elsewhere, and the share of turns with a music stop-down in the 2 s before against chance. Adds or updates one row per id in <data_folder>/staging.tsv.

payload.label: Sum a character's time in each video and set it against the video's views (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Sum how much a character speaks in each video of a show, in the opening, the body and the close, and see how that goes with how the videos did
payload.description: Per video with <data_folder>/voice/<id>.turns.json: turns, seconds, share, seconds in the opening (opening_seconds) and the close (closing_seconds), exchanges in the body (turns within 8 s) per ten minutes, median gap and turn, and whether it is one the character was stripped from (stripped_ids). Then, over the episodes: medians by year, the rank correlation of character seconds and share with views against the baseline per year and overall, the median against the baseline of the low, middle and high thirds by character seconds within each year, the stripped against the full episodes between compare_from_month and compare_to_month, and the episodes with the least character time from lowest_from_year. Writes <data_folder>/character-per-video.tsv.
